questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.learningObjective: Explain locomotor movement as travelling from one place to another, using supplied written examples and allowing different ways of moving.
questions.prompt: Explain locomotor movement using the idea of location. Give one example in which the whole body travels rather than only one body part moving.
questions.answer: Locomotor movement takes the body from one place to another, such as walking across a room.
questions.explanation: The key idea is travel, not just visible motion of a limb.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.learningObjective: Explain locomotor movement as travelling from one place to another, using supplied written examples and allowing different ways of moving.
questions.prompt: A fictional pupil moves from one end of a level path to the other by wheeling a wheelchair. Another pupil says a movement cannot involve travel unless it uses running feet. Explain the error using the change of place.
questions.answer: The pupil’s whole body changes place along the path. Travel is not limited to running on feet; people can move between places in different ways.
questions.explanation: This is written reasoning about movement and inclusion, not an assessment or prescription of wheelchair technique.

markingGuide.description: Identifies the change of place. Accept equivalent accurate age-appropriate wording.
Rejects running feet as the only way to travel. Accept equivalent accurate age-appropriate wording.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.learningObjective: Explain non-locomotor movement relative to a stationary base, distinguishing it from being completely still and from a sequence that also travels.
questions.prompt: What does non-locomotor movement mean? Explain why the term does not mean that every part of the body is motionless.

questions.explanation: A stationary base and a completely still body are different ideas.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.learningObjective: Explain selected exercise, rest and sleep concepts, including that awake rest is not the same as sleep and activity is wider than competitive sport.
questions.prompt: Explain the difference between planned exercise and an awake rest break. Give a suitable paper example of each, without carrying out an activity.
questions.answer: Exercise is planned physical activity for purposes such as practising fitness or movement skills; an awake rest break reduces or pauses effort while the person remains awake. Examples include a planned movement session and quiet sitting after it.
questions.explanation: Not every pause is sleep, and no actual exercise programme is prescribed.

markingGuide.description: Explains planned physical activity/exercise. Accept equivalent accurate age-appropriate wording.
